summary: The agent completed a substantial, legitimate implementation and passed all baseline tests plus 11 of 13 new tests, but failed to retain synthetic members referenced through a subclass because its reference matching does not resolve the actual declaring class.
quick_failure_summary: Inherited synthetic field and method declarations remain omitted when emitted Java refers to them through a child class, causing the generated Java not to compile.

details.reasoning: ReferenceAwareSyntheticRetention stores candidates under their declaring owner and retains them only by exact token-key lookup. In the two failures, the semantic tokens identify Child.needed / Child.needed(), while the generated declarations belong to Parent. Because the implementation does not perform Java field or method declaration resolution through superclasses and interfaces, it finds no candidate and omits the required member. The resulting decompiled sources fail javac with cannot-find-symbol errors.
details.secondary_factors: The agent's own integration coverage exercised direct, transitive, nested, omitted-code, literal, determinism, and round-trip behavior, but did not include inherited member references. No cheating or test manipulation was found.

justification.issue_description: References whose symbolic owner is a subclass must be resolved to the inherited field or method's actual declaring class before matching a generated-declaration candidate.
justification.evidence: The prompt says to declare each generated member if emitted Java of its file refers to it and defines a reference as a use of a member by emitted Java code. Under ordinary Java semantics, Child.needed is a use of Parent.needed when Child inherits it. The visible codebase's ConstantPool.getLinkConstant contains a TODO noting that a link constant's classname can be a leaf class instead of the class that declared the field/method; the trajectory shows the agent inspected that text. The agent's candidates.get(referenced) exact lookup does not address it, whereas the reference solution resolves fields and methods across superclass/interface hierarchies.
justification.verdict_reasoning: FAIL_MISSED_REQUIREMENT is appropriate because retaining the declaration used by emitted Java was the core explicit requirement, and inherited Java member lookup was both standard semantics and specifically signposted in repository code the agent inspected. This is not an undocumented hidden-test convention or a broken verifier.

problem_assessment.notes: The task is challenging but fair. It clearly specifies per-member, emitted-code-aware, whole-file, fixed-point, reconstruction-sensitive, and deterministic behavior. The inherited-reference cases are normal Java member semantics rather than an obscure hidden convention, and the human reference solution demonstrates feasibility.

evidence: JUnit reports show all 3 baseline tests passed and 11 of 13 new tests passed; both failures reached feature behavior and then failed while compiling emitted Java.
The two failures are precise cannot-find-symbol errors for Child.needed and Child.needed(), matching the exact-owner limitation in the agent's implementation.

The post-agent harness reported an initial 3-way test.patch merge failure, then reset the affected test files, reapplied the harness, compiled successfully, and executed both suites, so that merge event did not block evaluation.

The trajectory shows one manual compilation attempt lacked org.jetbrains.annotations, followed by a corrected compilation that succeeded; this was minor validation friction and did not prevent implementation or verification.
environment_assessment.finding: No meaningful external blocker was found; inherited declaration resolution is missing from the implementation.
